topic: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 vs LangGraph vs CrewAI: Which to Choose?

competitors.title: Definitive Guide to Agentic Frameworks in 2026: LangGraph, CrewAI, AG2, OpenAI and more
key_points: LangGraph: graph-based state machines, 25K GitHub stars, MIT license, Python+JS/TS, best for production stateful workflows with durable execution and human-in-the-loop
CrewAI: pre-assembled role-based multi-agent framework, 44.6K GitHub stars (most of any framework), Python only, best for rapid multi-agent prototyping with visual editor
AG2 (formerly AutoGen): conversation-based multi-agent paradigm, ~4.2K GitHub stars, Apache 2.0, best for research/experimentation but not production-ready
OpenAI Agents SDK: 5 primitives (Agents, Handoffs, Guardrails, Sessions, Tracing), 19.1K stars, built-in tools (web search, file search, computer use), best for OpenAI ecosystem
Pydantic AI: type-safe production agents, 15.1K stars, 25+ providers, MIT license, best for teams valuing code quality and output validation
Google ADK: multi-language (Python/TS/Go/Java), 18K stars, best for Google Cloud native and JVM teams
Amazon Bedrock Agents: fully managed AWS service, strongest security story, least flexibility, best for AWS enterprises

competitors.title: Build agents you can trust across any framework with open evals and a control standard (Microsoft Build 2026)
key_points: Microsoft announced ASSERT: open-source policy-driven agent evaluation framework, works across LangChain, CrewAI, LiteLLM, OpenAI
Microsoft announced Agent Control Specification (ACS): open standard for placing safety controls at 5 validation checkpoints (input, LLM, state, tool execution, output)
ACS partners include KPMG, Zscaler, Arize AI, IBM, CrewAI, Obsidian — built for ecosystem-wide adoption
Foundry Agent Service supports both prompt agents (fully managed) and hosted agents (code-based with Agent Framework, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Anthropic Agent SDK, etc.)
Foundry supports A2A protocol for agent-to-agent communication, MCP for tool interoperability
Guided Guardrail Setup in Foundry now in public preview — personalized guardrail recommendations in minutes
Rubric evaluator and multi-turn evaluation now in public preview for production agent quality monitoring
New Agent Optimizer closes the loop from production signal to continuous improvement

competitors.title: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service - Agent Framework official docs
key_points: Agent Framework is an open-source SDK for building hosted agents, part of Microsoft Foundry platform
Foundry supports ANY agent framework: Agent Framework, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Anthropic Agent SDK, GitHub Copilot SDK, or custom code
Two agent types: Prompt agents (fully managed, no runtime code) and Hosted agents (your code in containers, Foundry-managed)
Hosted agents support automatic scaling, dedicated Entra identity, session state persistence, end-to-end observability
Built-in tools: web search, file search, code interpreter, memory, MCP servers, SharePoint, WorkIQ, Fabric IQ
Enterprise security: Microsoft Entra identity, RBAC, content filters, virtual network isolation, Runtime DLP
Cost model: per-call inference + tool usage (+ container compute for hosted agents)

angles: Three-way showdown: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 (new enterpriser) vs LangGraph (production workhorse) vs CrewAI (rapid prototyping champion)
What Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 actually is: a hosted-agent platform that supports ANY framework — it's not competing with LangGraph, it's running on top of it
Framework choice framework: LangGraph for stateful production workflows, CrewAI for speed-to-deployment, Agent Framework for Azure-native enterprise teams
The enterprise convergence: How ASSERT, ACS, and Foundry's trust lifecycle make Microsoft the agent governance leader in 2026
Adoption-to-production gap: 51% deployed but only 1 in 9 in production — which framework gives the best path to production?
Cost reality: Framework setup ($50-100K) vs traditional automation ($500K-1M) — LangGraph's LangSmith ($39/seat) vs CrewAI Enterprise ($25+/month) vs Foundry per-call pricing
MCP as table stakes: By mid-2026, all three frameworks support MCP — differentiation moves to governance, observability, and managed infrastructure
Open-source vs managed: LangGraph and CrewAI are open-source (MIT), Agent Framework is Apache 2.0 — but Foundry is the managed platform layer above all three

The build-it-yourself vs buy-it debate: LangGraph's graph abstraction gives full control (more code), CrewAI's role-based model gives speed (less control), Agent Framework gives managed infra (vendor lock-in)
outline: Introduction: The agent framework explosion of 2026 — why three options stand out
Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0: What actually shipped (hosted agents, prompt agents, Foundry platform)
LangGraph 2026 overview: Graph-based state machines, durable execution, LangSmith observability
CrewAI 2026 overview: Role-based multi-agent, visual Studio editor, enterprise platform
Head-to-head comparison: Architecture philosophy, ease of use, production readiness, enterprise security
Microsoft's unique position: Framework-agnostic platform (runs LangGraph/CrewAI as hosted agents) + governance (ASSERT/ACS) + enterprise infrastructure
Production readiness analysis: 51% deployed, 1 in 9 in production — which framework closes the gap?
Cost comparison: LangGraph free + LangSmith $39/seat, CrewAI free to $25+/mo enterprise, Foundry per-call inference + tool usage
Use case decision matrix: Stateful workflows → LangGraph, Rapid prototyping → CrewAI, Azure-native → Agent Framework, Multi-language → Google ADK, Code quality → Pydantic AI
MCP and interoperability: How standards are reducing switching costs across Agent Framework, LangGraph, CrewAI
Enterprise governance: ASSERT open-source eval, Agent Control Specification, Foundry's trust lifecycle
Real-world case studies: Klarna (LangGraph), CrewAI (12M+ daily executions), Microsoft Foundry (enterprise deployments)

Conclusion: The right framework depends on your team, stack, and risk tolerance — but Microsoft's platform approach means you can start anywhere and converge
